subject.title: fix(msteams): add timeouts to SharePoint file send requests

question: Should MS Teams adopt the five-minute plus 256 KiB/s transfer deadline for both SharePoint upload paths, and which overlapping PR should establish the shared helper first?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically sound, but the minimum-throughput cutoff can intentionally fail very slow existing uploads, and two open PRs currently claim the same canonical helper.

options.title: Land file consent first
options.body: Land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104120 as the narrower shared-helper change, then refresh this PR to consume that helper and remove duplicate policy churn.

options.title: Land this PR first
options.body: Accept this PR as the shared-helper owner, then refresh the file-consent PR to use the implementation established here.

options.title: Pause both for tenant proof
options.body: Hold both PRs until a live Microsoft tenant validates slow success and timeout failure under representative upload conditions.

recommendation.title: Land file consent first
recommendation.body: Land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104120 as the narrower shared-helper change, then refresh this PR to consume that helper and remove duplicate policy churn.

likelyOwner.reason: The published MS Teams plugin ownership signal makes this the best available routing candidate for accepting the compatibility cutoff and merge order.
